items.title: Deep Learning-Driven Distributed PV Segmentation & Thermal Impact Assessment
items.description: Applied the SegUNet++ semantic segmentation framework to sub-meter UAV imagery to map distributed rooftop PV across two Dutch cities, supported by LiDAR point density visualization to inspect 3D terrain features and Landsat-8 TIRS to assess local surface warming effects.

items.title: Causal Attribution of Urban Thermal Dynamics Using TsHARP-Downscaled LST
items.description: Integrated multi-source data (GAIA, GHSL) to delineate precise urban boundaries in Madrid, and independently downscaled 2025 Landsat LST to 10 m via the TsHARP algorithm. Quantified thermal heterogeneity (2009–2025) via multiple UHI indices (URI, SUHII), and paired Random Forest with GPS-based causal inference to decouple the warming footprint of population expansion from topographic confounders.

items.title: Spatiotemporal Evaluation and Driver Attribution of Urban Ecological Quality
items.description: Evaluated multi-temporal (2003, 2014, 2024) ecological dynamics across Greater Vancouver by extracting the remote sensing based ecological index (RSEI) via Principal Component Analysis (PCA) in Google Earth Engine. Conducted spatial statistics and correlation analysis to reveal a distinct "South-Poor, North-Good" ecological gradient, identifying vegetation (NDVI, R^2 ≈ 0.9) as the dominant positive driver offsetting the degradation footprint from urban heat and built-up expansion.

items.title: Impacts of 3D Urban Morphology and Blue-Green Spaces on the Urban Thermal Environment
items.description: Conducted a comparative geospatial analysis of the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect across Fuzhou and Singapore by integrating Landsat-8 land surface temperature (LST) with Local Climate Zone (LCZ) classifications. Deployed Moran’s I spatial clustering and Random Forest regression to quantify thermal heterogeneity, revealing that while Fuzhou's LST is primarily mitigated by the spatial extent and connectivity of blue-green patches, Singapore's thermal patterns are dominantly governed by 3D architectural zoning (LCZs) and the clustering of vegetation.

items.title: Cross-Biome Validation of Red-Edge Vegetation Indices via GF-6 Satellite Imagery
items.description: Evaluated the cross-regional robustness of six red-edge vegetation indices (e.g., NDRE1, REP, IRECI) for forest health classification across the Rocky Mountains (USA) and Kaçkar Mountains (Turkey). Processed 16m GaoFen-6 (GF-6) WFV imagery, executing R-based boxplot statistical analysis to dynamically delineate vegetation vitality thresholds, alongside custom ArcPy scripts for automated multi-point extraction and confusion matrix validation. Quantified significant algorithmic sensitivity to diverse biomes, identifying NDRE1 and REP as the optimal indices for dry-alpine and humid-temperate ecosystems, respectively (achieving up to 84.4% overall accuracy).

items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Atmospheric Correction Models for GF-6 Imagery Across Subtropical Ecosystems
items.description: Evaluated the spectral consistency of FLAASH and the Image-based Atmospheric Correction Model (IACM) using 16 m GaoFen-6 (GF-6) WFV imagery across the Xishuangbanna and Wuyishan Nature Reserves. Built a preprocessing pipeline integrating orthorectification, radiometric calibration, and BandMath programming to compute surface reflectance based on solar zenith angles and darkest-pixel atmospheric correction. Conducted spectral consistency analysis, revealing that while both models effectively resolve terrain shadows, IACM demonstrates superior spectral restoration for vegetation, better preserving the green peak and red-edge rise in vegetation spectra.

about.title: About Me
about.intro: Hi, I'm <1>Claire</1>,  a postgraduate student at Fuzhou University pursuing a Master's degree in Cartography and Geographic Information Systems. My core research interests lie at the intersection of spatial data science, renewable energy mapping, and remote sensing ecology.
about.paragraph1: My current research focuses on the automated extraction of photovoltaic (PV) facilities and the systematic evaluation of their ecological and thermal environmental effects. By leveraging multi-source earth observation data (such as Landsat, Sentinel-2, and sub-meter UAV imagery), I map solar infrastructure across diverse landscapes—from distributed urban rooftops to utility-scale solar farms in arid deserts and high-altitude plateaus. I aim to quantify how large-scale renewable energy deployment reshapes local microclimates and ecological gradients.
about.paragraph2: My work combines spatial analysis, remote sensing image processing, machine learning, deep learning, and cloud-native computing. These methods allow me to examine environmental dynamics at multiple spatial and temporal scales, from the local thermal effects of distributed rooftop photovoltaics to the regional ecological impacts of utility-scale solar farms. I hope to contribute to a better understanding of the environmental impacts of renewable energy expansion and to support more sustainable land-use planning and ecological decision-making.
